group.title: Society and the world
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: To give reasons to show that something is true or false.
examples: Some people {argue} that homework is helpful.
wrong: He argues the table with milk.
I argued of the idea.

words.meaning: A good result or advantage.
examples: One {benefit} of exercise is better sleep.
wrong: One benefit of the storm is that it destroyed our roof.
He benefits of a lot.

words.meaning: A series of steps that lead to a result.
examples: Making cheese is a long {process}.
wrong: The process has no steps and no end.
He process the milk for cheese.

words.meaning: To look at things to see how they are alike or different.
examples: Let’s {compare} the two phones before we buy one.
wrong: I compare one phone without looking at the other.
She compares at the prices.

words.meaning: To make something new.
examples: Artists {create} new things every day.
wrong: I created a painting that already existed.
She creates of a song.

words.meaning: The group of people that rules a country.
examples: The {government} plans to build new schools.
wrong: A government is a small shop that sells food.

words.meaning: A time when people vote to choose a leader.
examples: The {election} will be held in November.
wrong: An election is a holiday when no one votes.

words.meaning: A person who legally belongs to a country.
examples: Every {citizen} has the right to vote.
wrong: A citizen is a tourist who stays for one day only.

words.meaning: A rule made by a government that people must follow.
examples: It is against the {law} to drive without a license.
wrong: A law is a rule that nobody has to follow.

words.meaning: An act that breaks the law.
examples: Theft is a {crime}.
wrong: A crime is a kind of sport.

words.meaning: Dirt or harmful things in the air, water or land.
examples: {Pollution} from cars makes the air dirty.
wrong: Pollution is clean air in the mountains.

words.meaning: The natural world, including land, water and air.
examples: We must protect the {environment}.
wrong: The environment is a building made of glass.

words.meaning: The usual weather in a place over a long time.
examples: The {climate} in this country is hot and dry.
wrong: The climate is the weather you have only today at ten o’clock.

words.meaning: To treat old things so that they can be used again.
examples: We {recycle} paper and glass.
wrong: I recycle a bottle by throwing it in the river.

words.meaning: To keep someone or something safe from harm.
examples: Trees {protect} the soil from the wind.
wrong: I protect my phone by dropping it on the street.

words.meaning: The number of people who live in a place.
examples: The {population} of the city is two million.
wrong: The population is the number of cars that a company makes.

words.meaning: The state of being very poor.
examples: Many families live in {poverty}.
wrong: Poverty is the state of having a great deal of money.

words.meaning: A person who comes to live in a different country.
examples: My grandfather was an {immigrant} from Italy.
wrong: An immigrant is a person who never leaves their home town.

words.meaning: The way of life, art and customs of a group of people.
examples: I like learning about other {cultures}.
wrong: A culture is a machine for making coffee.

words.meaning: A custom that has been passed on for a long time.
examples: It is a {tradition} to eat rice cake at New Year.
wrong: A tradition is a new idea that started yesterday.

words.meaning: A system of belief in a god or gods.
examples: {Religion} is important to many people.
wrong: Religion is a sport that people play in a stadium.

words.meaning: A situation in which everyone has the same rights.
examples: They are working for {equality} between men and women.
wrong: Equality means that some people have more rights than others.

words.meaning: The right to do what you want.
examples: Everyone should have {freedom} of speech.
wrong: Freedom means you cannot make any choices.

words.meaning: What you think about something.
examples: In my {opinion}, the film was too long.
wrong: An opinion is a fact that everyone must accept.

words.meaning: Newspapers, television and the internet that give people news.
examples: The {media} reported the story the same day.
wrong: The media is a place where people buy shoes.

words.meaning: A notice that tries to make people buy something.
examples: I saw an {advertisement} for a new phone.
wrong: An advertisement is a message that tells people not to buy anything.

words.meaning: A famous person.
examples: The {celebrity} signed autographs outside the theater.
wrong: A celebrity is a person whom nobody knows.

words.meaning: The power to change what people think or do.
examples: Her parents had a strong {influence} on her.
wrong: Influence is the lack of any power over others.

words.meaning: Behavior that is meant to hurt other people.
examples: The film contains a lot of {violence}.
wrong: Violence is the act of helping other people politely.

words.meaning: Fair treatment under the law.
examples: The family wanted {justice} for the victim.
wrong: Justice is the unfair treatment of people without rules.

words.meaning: A person who works without pay because they want to.
examples: A {volunteer} helped me find the room.
wrong: A volunteer is a person who is paid a high salary and is forced to work.

words.meaning: An organization that gives help to people who need it.
examples: They gave the money to a {charity}.
wrong: A charity is a company that makes money only for its owner.

words.meaning: To give money or things to help others.
examples: I want to {donate} some clothes.
wrong: I donate a book to a friend when I sell it for a high price.

words.meaning: Money that people pay to the government.
examples: We pay {tax} on the things we earn.
wrong: Tax is money the government pays to every person at the shop.

words.meaning: The system of money, trade and jobs in a country.
examples: The {economy} grew by two percent last year.
wrong: The economy is the system of roads in a city.

words.meaning: The business of making goods in factories.
examples: The car {industry} employs many people.
wrong: Industry is the activity of sleeping all day.

words.meaning: Machines and methods that use scientific knowledge.
examples: New {technology} makes work faster.
wrong: Technology is a kind of old food.

words.meaning: All the people who live in a country or community.
examples: A fair {society} protects its weakest members.
wrong: Society is one person alone on an island.

words.meaning: The power to give orders or make decisions.
examples: The police have the {authority} to stop cars.
wrong: Authority is the lack of any power to decide.

words.meaning: An event where people show they disagree with something.
examples: Hundreds joined the {protest} against the new tax.
wrong: A protest is a party where everyone agrees and no one speaks.
